en: I am truly sorry, Lord Leviathan. Your greatness is outmatched only by your fury, and that fury cannot be left unchecked. Pray go peacefully.

I came here at my Lady Wife's bidding, to try and broker a deal with Leviathan, a divine creature that dwells 'neath our island. There are many centuries of history between the royal family and he, and we thought to seek his aid.

I cannot say whether you are defiant or simply incapable, but it scarcely matters. You have put an end to a unique and beautiful creature who frankly had more of a right to exist than you do. And for what? The short, furtive life of a fugitive?

I have disturbed the delicate harmony of the holy chains, and as such, they will crumble when struck. The chains are anchored at fifteen points throughout this temple. Destroy those, and he will be able to slip free of the remaining chain on his own.

I have tried to speak with him, to inform him of our plan and spare you the rigors of combat, but the chains dull my voice. He knows only rage, hears no reason, and he will lash out at every turn. Break his arms if you must, but leave him alive.

I see. Well, I suppose that's the best team you could put together, given the circumstances. It will have to do. 
Now, enough chit-chat.
I understand that I have harmed you and killed many others, that I have injured this island that I love. You have repaid my savagery with kindness and mercy. I am humbled, utterly.
I'll be watching.
I, however, have many reasons. Clear the noise, and let us make him listen.

If you enter here, do it to destroy him. I drew his blood myself, so I am certain he can be slain. Alas, my fellows were cut down, and I was mortally wounded. There is little more I can do but pen this warning with my final hours.
Leviathan. You killed Maxim, and his revenge is long overdue! Slip back into the deep, and never return!
Mayhap Fastad's endeavor will bear sweeter fruit. Mine tastes only of blood.
My brother. I saw you only weeks ago, and now to find you like this, hundreds of years slain.

Now here's an interesting choice. Oh don't fret, she can't see me either, but I bet she is itching insufferably right about now. I'm also not sure how you managed to convince a pretend servant of god to turn her weapon against a legitimate one, but good job on that. Take advantage of her conviction. That's about all she'll be good for.

Now there's a solid choice! Bring the relic who should never have been here in the first place. He is meant to be ages dead already, so if he dies, nothing is lost, and if he brings you victory, so much the better. This tells me you're someone with an eye for managing risk. Good! I like that.

Now there's a solid choice, the dancing assassin! She did tell you she's an assassin, right? Lots of tricks up her sleeve, and up her skirt too, no doubt. I suspect she'll serve well in this fight, but you'd best not trust her. Who knows what she'll do when the danger's past?

Of all goblins, you had to choose that one, the one with the literal addiction to jewelry? Even if he makes a name for himself in this battle, it will be a name unsung both by his kind and by yours. He knows this. Do you think his heart is really in this fight? Can you afford to take that chance?
Of course it had to be a giant fish. Why wouldn't it be a giant fish? Just... just don't leave me alone, okay? I can't die here, not like this!
Oh to raise arms against you Lord Leviathan! I would have been your disciple if not for such rage!
Oh, fuck me! We really gotta fight this thing? This ain't gonna be fun, boys and girls.
Oh, goodness. He doesn't look comfortable. Or happy to see us, for that matter. We're in it now.
Once all of the anchors are broken, I will be able to speak clearly with him, soothe his rage, and negotiate our terms.
Pff, he don't look so tough. I can still smell his blood, still hear his heart, and if he's got a heart, then it can be cut out. Come lay down for your end, you damn eel.
Shame he had such trouble thinking outside of his tiny little box. He could not reason with Leviathan because he could offer Leviathan no reason to listen.
So this is what's left of the fabled hero, Maxim Spartill? I'd have liked to meet him. I understand that in life he was powerful, beautiful, and charismatic.
Sorry, Daddy, but you're not doing the world any favors the way you are now. If it's gotta be you or us, it's gonna be you!
Such a magnificent creature! I'm rather dismayed that we'll have to destroy it.

Take your freedom then, since you desire it so badly, and leave the island to mourn its father. 

He will stir the seas nevermore.

The Left-Leaning Monster? Interesting choice, though I'd have expected someone with such a violent reputation to be a bit more violent. He might not be as useful as you'd think, unless you're planning to hide behind him.

The Muffin Mage. 
Really? You didn't want someone with a little more arcane fire in the belly? Maybe you just have a hardon for making things difficult? I suppose he'll at least taste good when Leviathan eats him.

The best things about wild, axe-swinging barbarians are the deep belly-laughing when the fight is over, the drinking and the sweat and the skin when the fire is low, the warmth that burns behind the violence. This one is none of those things. She might win the fight for you, but she isn't your friend.

The dead cannot be assuaged, but to you, I shall attempt to make amends. I am bound no longer, and I'll dare not subject myself to such bonds again, but I will bequeath this island to you, and for a time, I shall stir the seas to your favor.

The men I brought were skilled individually, but there was no bond of trust between us, and Leviathan tossed us aside easily. I wish Luc and Fastad had been here. I always felt like the three of us could accomplish anything together.
This is a divine beast? What a bitter disappointment. I'll slay this one no different than a thousand others I've slain.
This one'll be a story for the kids I'll never get to have! The day Daddy took down the biggest boss of the sea!

Ugh, are you still dragging that thing around? You know that zombies are supposed to be temporary, right? It stinks, and you should get rid of it. Though, come to think of it, bringing it in here probably will be getting rid of it, so... good job!
Well damn, that's a big boy. How many steaks you think we'll get out of that?
Well shit, he definitely looks like he lifts. I suppose pulling against divine chains for centuries will do that to a guy.

Well this is disappointing. A common burglar. He does have an uncommonly nice body though, so I suppose I can't fault you for wanting him along, but you might have done better to let the pretty ones wait outside while you take care of the real work. It would be a shame if he ends up broken. You might want to use him later.
Well, win or lose it's been quite a trip. I'd really prefer win though, so sorry big guy, but you're going down!
What a brutal disappointment. That brand you wear is a pale shade next to the crime you have just committed. Is mercy truly so far outside of your understanding?
What a perverted destination this road holds. I wanted to keep decent people safe, and now I must war against a creature of God? Heaven help us all.

While I approve of giants in general, you could've chosen one more battle-minded. Leviathan is not some towering oak to be felled by the hands of a scruffy, overmuscled labourer, though that does conjure an interesting mental picture. You'd best be sure his axe is sharp enough, or you'll fall beside him.

Who has more rage at the servants of god than a cursed child of blood and darkness? The bitter unfairness of it all must be positively bursting inside his cold, dead chest. If he survives this, he'll probably fancy himself the most powerful vampire on the island. Maybe he'll even be right.
Why did I let you drag me into this? I should've just found somewhere warm and dry and... well it's too late for that, I guess. Let's get this over with.
Yes, that's right, my Leviathan. Breathe out your rage and relax. You must be so very tired.
You know, he's curiously attractive for a fish man. Wasn't expecting that. Too bad about the whole murderous rage thing, that really makes it hard to focus on the positives. Sorry, pops.

You're really pulling out all the stops by bringing the werewolf, aren't you? He's certainly got spit and rage enough, and I can well-appreciate a man whose body betrays his love of base indulgence. Hopefully your victory is more important than his own pleasure in this case.
You're the one who denies me the open sea, denies me my freedom! No more, beast! Today we are taking it back!
You, who sundered my chains. Come and stand before me. You've nothing to fear.

Your companions can't see me or hear me, but that is a choice rather than a limitation. I understand that making a deal with a devil is something one might wish to keep... private. Let's see who you've decided to bring along.
Your quest is mine, Max. I will see this made right, and then I will see you put to rest. Wait for me.

barbarian types? I could tell. You must ensure that no matter what happens, that orc is never, ever allowed to wear a shirt. Write it into law if you must. Ensure that this one survives, will you? I couldn't bear to see him damaged.
Blood for Power
... I mean...
A favor?
And I don't want to.
Anyway, what's this about Leftie? Has he been bothering you?
But I can see that I'm going to change my mind, so do it anyway.
Do me a favor, Vankan?
Do you think I should tell him?
Don't want to? It's your fault for putting the idea in my head.
Good, you came. I really, really need-
He told me that night he committed buggery, rape, two murders, arson, and cannibalism. It was really hard for him to say it all.
Here I am.

His memory of that night is fragmented, incomplete, and patched with lazy guesses. He believes himself a horror so that he has someone close by to blame. To do otherwise would nurture a helpless rage, and of that he is more afraid.
I cannot help but notice. And there is more, besides.

I cannot say for certain what occurred there, but I am confident that only a single life was taken by his hand that night. The other life was taken by the woman. I suspect that some of the other details are wrong as well.
I do apologize if my letter gave you the wrong idea.
I don't really know. I just know that I was supposed to meet with you tonight, and we were meant to talk about Leftie. It feels like we've accomplished something, so perhaps that's it.
I don't see...
I just thought that note meant that you wanted to...
I know that he told you about the person he killed, and he thinks about it almost constantly.
I may not see everything, but what I see is the truth. Pray, what else did he say?
I really need to talk to you about Leftie.
I see.
I understand that you've become quite fond of clandestine encounters. You should come and find me when you wake.
I'm going back to bed. Thanks for the information.
It's Leftie's business, but if you've already got half of the picture...
It's fine, Vankan. I was jumping to conclusions.
More? What do you mean?
Nobody else will come this way tonight. We should be fine.
Not as such. I know that the two of you shared an intimate evening, whatever that entailed. That's not really a concern of mine, but ever since then, he thinks of you often, and intensely.
Of course. I'll be along in a few minutes.
Oh my. That's...
Oh no, wait, there's something...
Oh!
Oh.

Rest Stop. 

Free for all travellers, courtesy of the Gracious Lord Frico.
Seems clear.
So he thinks, but I assure you, he did not.
Someday, perhaps, but not now. The visions of the madman are hardly compelling proof besides. Leftie loves you because you accepted his flaws. He doesn't need absolution, not really.
The next hour? I'm not sure I can be that specific, but I'll try.
Try really hard to look into my future, will you? Specifically the next hour or so.
Wait, the person? Leftie told me he killed two people.
Well, there you have it. Make yourselves comfortable.
Well, this has been interesting. That was what you wanted to talk to me about?
Yes! Yes. It is my fault.
You seem disappointed.
Fastad, what have you done?
Forgive me. I believe you speak the truth, and I doubt you have the answers.
I took this place behind bars willingly, to absolve my Queen of wrongdoing, but I never expected to be chained by the stuff of time itself. It is... disconcerting.

My name is Luc Beauregard, former Knight-Captain in service of Her Royal Highness Queen Glamig Cosova. I guess none of that matters anymore though. My title was stripped when I came here, and now my kingdom and my world are gone. The bastard would have been kinder to let me die forgotten, as was my lot.
She is dead then. Long dead, if you are to be believed, along with Fastad and everyone else. I... why was I spared? What did that lunatic hope to accomplish by shielding me from the passage of time?

Still... I never did care much for giving up. Perhaps I'll venture forth to see what is left of the world I know. I'm afraid I have nothing to offer you as reward for releasing me, so I pray my thanks will suffice.
Time graces ungrateful mortals with its touch everlong. How dare you presume to demand it bend to your whims! Yours is an endeavor most forbidden, and your punishment is death!
You... you are not Fastad. Who are you? What is going on? What happened to him?

A corruption from beneath the earth has come to feed on the heart of this forest, and we were not strong enough to stop it. The monks who tended the temple, and the dryads who were their friends, all have fallen.
Begone, stranger. The temple is fallen, and there is nothing of beauty left.
Even its destruction, though, makes way for new life. The end meets the beginning, and life continues. This is the rhythm of the verdant vein.
Foolish flower! See what your treachery has wrought!
I alone was spared, and only so I could ward away travelers like you. Please, you must leave. Only the stone survives. At least this way, the corruption will spread no further.
Now suffer, as I have suffered, and perish!
Only the stone survives.
Suffer, as I have suffered, and perish!
Take then my first and surest seed. Hold my rhythm inside of you, and know forever the gratitude of my wood.
Take what is left of my power. This forest needs it no longer.
This place, this forest, it is mine! Ye who dare to challenge my stronghold are naught but dry leaves before a tide of flame!

This... do you truly walk with the blessing of the mountains themselves? You then, may stand a chance. Please, destroy the corruption inside, and put an end to all those who fell to it. I will open the way for you!

Though I am this day fallen, your victory clears way for my seed to rise again. It will take time, but the new forest will devour this corruption as the corruption has devoured me. This is the rhythm of the verdant vein.
You who have come to avenge this forest. Stand with pride before me, that I may honour your wounds as you have honored mine.
You who have come to cleanse this blight. You seek to save this forest, but it is beyond saving.
Finally, I am free!
A cage. I really don't like the look of this place. We'd best finish what we need to do and move on.
Anyway, thanks. I'll get out of your way.
Behind you, fool! It's a trap!

I'm Greave. Was working at the stocks for awhile, but I couldn't continue to be a part of that farce, so I left. Did alright for a week or so, until I got lured in by these damned hags. I really should've known better.
Nice bit of work, there. I am not sure how I would've got out of that one if you hadn't come along.
Ye who dare come to the heart of my coven, slaughter my sisters, and release my animals! You will surrender your eyes and your tongues in recompense!
You... you did it! Do you think you can get me out?
... eh, sorry. You live your whole life being treated like a monster and it's hard to let go of the old habits. I know we're all in this shit boat together.
Alright, well you work something out with the operator then, and let me know.
Anyway, sorry again for snapping at you. Don't fall off a cliff.

At least you'd think so. Not this asswipe though. I need to cross here, but I ain't got enough coin, and he isn't willing to do a guy a favor. I been stuck here all morning trying to figure out what to do. I guess I could climb, but it seems awful dangerous.
Did... you hear something just now? I could've sworn I heard something.
Do you see that? Are... are those people over there?
I guess I can hardly blame you for separating beauty from danger. Probably most people would agree with you.
I guess some folks are like that, and I won't say it's wrong. There are certainly some people on this island who rightly deserve to get their asses kicked.

I guess you've never had to live your life in darkness then, worrying that your neighbor might flash a smile to you by day and put a torch to you by night? It kinda gives a guy a different perspective on the world.

I know, right? Folks like us, we're better off without all these stupid rules and taboos holding us down, snuffing us out like we're not good enough to exist. Here, if you're strong and smart, you live, and if you're weak, you die. Simple.
I see something moving over there. Can you make out what that is?
I'm not really surprised to hear you say that. You struck me as that sort of person. I mean, you decided to help me out, when you really didn't have to, after all. That says a lot.

It's funny how you can sometimes find beauty in the most deadly things, isn't it? This island certainly has no shortage of those. Deadly things, I mean. Maybe I'm crazy for being okay with that, for taking in the beauty of it when I see it.

It's kinda pretty from a distance, but that was magic, wasn't it? Some desperate soul slinging the very breath of the world fighting for his life, probably. It stopped, so either he's dead or his enemies are.
Look, I ain't running a charity here. I want that guy gone, but I can't let you ride for free.
Nice try, but you need the full amount. Come back when your pockets are heavier.
Of course I am. Every fight, even a fight that you think you'll win, is a chance to die. If there's no need to take that chance, then why take it? Makes no sense.
